newsitem.title: JAPAN: Green Cross, Yoshitomi to announce delay in merger.
newsitem.headline: Green Cross, Yoshitomi to announce delay in merger.

text.p: Green Cross Corp and Yoshitomi Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd said on Wednesday that they would announce a postponement of their planned merger at 4.30 p.m. (0730 GMT).

Under the merger plan announced in February, Yoshitomi, a medium-sized Japanese drug company, was due to take over scandal-tainted Green Cross on October 1. Five shares of Green Cross were to be exchanged for three Yoshitomi shares.
Osaka-based Green Cross has been at the centre of a scandal concerning HIV-tainted blood products. Former Green Cross executives were indicted last October on charges of professional negligence.
Green Cross has seen a sharp fall in sales after public outrage over the scandal prompted boycotts of its products at many medical institutions.
The two firms said at that time that the new company would take over responsibility for compensation to victims of the tainted blood products, officials said.

Green Cross faces compensation payments totalling about 24 billion yen to people who were infected with HIV through the use of its blood products. The blood products were not heat-treated even though company documents showed that officials knew there was a risk that such unheated products could carry the virus that causes AIDS.
Yoshitomi's president Masashi Goya was due to take the helm of the new company, while Green Cross president Kazunari Doi was to assume the position of executive vice president.
The companies said that the merger was postponed because it would take more time than previously expected to hammer out an agreement on how the merged company would be operated.
